audit_findings.title: The valuation perimeter omits a post-year-end acquisition
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor excludes Hamm operating earnings and acquisition financing costs, while the valuation uses the June 2026 share count and balance-sheet context.
audit_findings.evidence: In February 2026, we acquired certain assets and assumed certain liabilities from Hamm, LLC, N.R. Hamm Quarry, LLC, N.R. Hamm Contractor, LLC, and Cornejo & Sons, LLC constituting a vertically-integrated recycling and waste business located in Kansas.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filing does not isolate Hamm's earnings, financing costs, purchase price, or shares attributable to the transaction. The $860 million aggregate purchase price for all first-half 2026 acquisitions and their aggregate 1.1% contribution to first-half revenue cannot establish Hamm's valuation effect. Omitting profitable acquired operations would understate value, while omitting associated interest and required investment would overstate it.
audit_findings.action: Calculate post-acquisition LTM OE with Hamm revenue, operating costs, maintenance investment, taxes, and financing costs, then rerun; alternatively use FY2025-period shares and bridge inputs consistently.

audit_findings.title: The $400 million stakes addition may double-count tax-equity economics
audit_findings.magnitude: $400 million bridge addition; 2025 capital contributions $227 million, tax benefits $175 million, and HLBV carrying-value reduction $135 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Investment-related losses and tax benefits enter OE, contributions affect cash required from owners, and the investment carrying value is separately added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, our tax provisions reflect benefits of approximately $ 175 million and $ 222 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, due to tax credits net of nondeductible items, related to these investments.
audit_findings.explanation: Double-counting is not yet demonstrated because the OE adjustments underlying the $2,333.9 million anchor are not supplied. The filed flows are nevertheless large relative to the anchor: the $175 million tax benefit equals 7.5% and the $227 million contribution equals 9.7%. The HLBV loss can depress OE while retained tax benefits and omitted contributions can inflate it, so the net direction cannot be established without tracing the components. This scale is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each investment comprising stakes_net to its carrying value, HLBV income or loss, tax credits, contributions, distributions, and OE adjustments; rerun using either a wholly inside-OE or wholly bridge-based treatment.

audit_findings.title: Landfill retirement obligations require an explicit OE-to-cash reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.313 billion accrued obligation; 2025 cash expenditures $70 million; 2025 landfill retirement amortization $114 million and accretion $114 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Landfill amortization and accretion reduce reported earnings, while capping, closure, and post-closure expenditures consume cash; inappropriate expense add-backs or inadequate maintenance deductions overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our future obligations for final capping, closure and post-closure costs totaled $2.3 billion, of which $87 million was short-term.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial operating obligations but does not demonstrate that the valuation mishandled them because the OE worksheet is absent. The two relevant 2025 expenses total $228 million, or 9.8% of anchor OE, and are therefore capable of materially changing value if added back without an offsetting normalized cash requirement. The $2.313 billion liability is already accrued accounting cost, so it should not automatically be deducted again if OE properly retains the associated economics.
audit_findings.action: Map the OE calculation to the $114 million amortization, $114 million accretion, $70 million cash expenditure, landfill development capital, and asset-retirement adjustments; rerun only for expenses added back without a corresponding normalized cash deduction.

audit_findings.title: Potential remediation claims exceed recorded liabilities
audit_findings.magnitude: $276 million, equal to $0.89 per diluted share and 0.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any amount above the recorded remediation liability would reduce future OE when paid or enter the equity bridge as an additional senior operating claim.
audit_findings.evidence: If we used the reasonably possible high ends of our ranges, our aggregate potential remediation liability as of December 31, 2025 would be approximately $ 276 million higher than the amounts recorded.
audit_findings.explanation: The additional $276 million is a filed reasonably possible high-end amount, not a demonstrated liability. Even deducting the full amount immediately would reduce value by only $0.89 per share, versus scenario values of $91.45 to $141.28 and a market price of $223.72. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Retain the contingency schedule and update the bridge only if later filings establish a probable amount above the recorded liability or materially increase the reasonably possible range.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor includes disaster-driven revenue
audit_findings.magnitude: $100 million of 2025 revenue; computed maximum anchor sensitivity of $3.85 to $5.98 per share if all revenue were treated as OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrecurring after-tax profit embedded in FY2025 OE inflates the anchor and is then grown and capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: These events increased revenue during 2025 by approximately $100 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $100 million nonrecurring revenue is demonstrated, but an OE error is not because associated operating costs and elevated landfill depletion were recorded. As a conservative upper bound, treating the entire $100 million of revenue as removable OE would lower the bear, base, and bull values by approximately $3.85, $5.36, and $5.98 per share. Actual profit impact must be smaller than this revenue-only bound, so it cannot bridge the $82.44 per-share gap between bull value and market price or change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the disaster work's revenue, direct costs, landfill depletion, maintenance investment, and taxes; normalize the FY2025 anchor if its actual after-tax OE contribution was retained.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded multiemployer pension exposure is not quantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rehabilitation contributions would reduce OE, while a withdrawal or mass-withdrawal liability could require a bridge deduction or scenario cash outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: We cannot presently determine the amount of additional funding, if any, we may be required to make to these plans.
audit_findings.explanation: No additional obligation is presently quantified or demonstrated. The latest filing continues to carry a $20 million withdrawal liability, and the principal disclosed plan was in the safe zone, but the record cannot bound exposure for the other plans. This is a forward-looking contingent claim rather than a presently measurable valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current funding notices, rehabilitation plans, employer-allocation data, and withdrawal-liability estimates; reassess when an additional contribution schedule or probable withdrawal claim becomes measurable.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2019 residual $81.9 million; computed current anchor effect $0
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A left as an expense understates historical OE and could raise the fitted trend if later supported, but the valuation anchors at the lower FY2025 actual OE.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $81.9m (7.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative rather than an overstatement. The supplied residual concerns FY2019 and could affect the historical trend, but the $2,333.9 million FY2025 actual already binds because it is $113.1 million below the $2,447 million trend. Therefore the stated anchoring rule gives the FY2019 residual no current valuation effect.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2019 residual only if filed evidence supports an eligible non-economic add-back; rerun the trend and confirm whether the latest-actual cap still binds.
